correctness.rationale: The published Fermat description gives 55 smooth reduced components indexed by 2+4 and 3+3 coordinate-support splittings. A point lies on multiple such components exactly when a coordinate vanishes on the represented line, so the reduced union is singular precisely on that coordinate-degeneration locus. On each block component, Zhang's higher-triple second-order matrix splits into the Fermat block second fundamental forms; their Hessians have determinant proportional to the product of block coordinates, so the higher-triple condition is the same coordinate-vanishing condition. The independent symbolic verifier confirms the r=3 and r=4 Hessian determinants and exhaustively verifies the finite counts 180 curves, 405 deep points, nine incidences per curve and four curves per deep point.

originality.rationale: Zhang defines higher triple lines, records at least 45 one-parameter Fermat families and explicitly asks how higher triple lines relate to singularities of F2 in dimension at least four. Gounelas–Kouvidakis give the complete reduced Fermat second-type decomposition into 45 cubic surfaces and 10 products of Fermat plane cubics, but do not identify its singular locus with higher triple lines or give the 180/405 incidence refinement. The audited block-Hessian comparison joins those ingredients and answers Zhang's question for this canonical special fourfold. No independent Resultary theorem was found.

value.rationale: The result answers an explicit recent question for a canonical highly symmetric cubic fourfold, identifies two independently defined geometric loci and upgrades the previously noted Fermat families to a complete elliptic-component and incidence classification. This is a natural structural special case rather than a gratuitous finite computation.
residual_risks: An equivalent special-case computation could exist under different Fano-locus terminology.
The theorem is only set-theoretic on the reduced second-type locus and does not determine local analytic branch multiplicities.

final_claim: For the Fermat cubic fourfold, the higher triple lines are exactly the singular locus of the reduced second-type line locus; this common set is the union of 180 smooth Fermat elliptic curves meeting only at 405 deep lines, with nine deep points on each curve and four curves through each deep point.
limitations: Set-theoretic equality for the reduced second-type locus only; no scheme multiplicities, local analytic type or transversality claim.
